**Why reflow ovens must be switched off:**
According to SOP-02, a reflow oven left in standby draws 36% of its 70 kW rating (25.2 kW) continuously. In contrast, a properly switched-off oven uses only about 340–350 kWh over a weekend. Leaving it in standby is the largest single source of idle weekend energy [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

**Excess energy cost in incident S5:**
In incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20), reflow oven RF-02 was left in standby. The document states this resulted in about **1,210 kWh** of excess energy compared to normal operation [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

Based on the actual energy data for RF-02 during this period (1,976.9 kWh costing NT$6,045), the average rate was approximately NT$3.06/kWh [data: get_energy]. Therefore, the cost of the excess energy was approximately **NT$3,702** (1,210 kWh × NT$3.06/kWh).

According to the demand-exceedance procedure:

**First load shed:** EV charging (EV-01) is paused first, as it has no effect on production [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook].

**Loads that must never be shed:**
- Server room (DC-01)
- Running molders mid-cycle (IM-01 to IM-04)
- Reflow ovens with boards inside (RF-01 to RF-03) [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]
